question.value: Determine mass-loss rates and mm properties of the post-main-sequence massive stars (WR, OB super/hypergiants, cool hypergiants) in the cluster Westerlund 1 from a 3 mm ALMA continuum census

evidence.quote: We aim to study the constituent stars of the Galactic cluster Westerlund 1 in order to determine mass-loss rates for the diverse post-main sequence population of massive stars.

findings_qualitative.value: All 21 WRs in the field detected; many hot stars appear spatially resolved; cool hypergiants show cometary nebulae oriented away from cluster core

evidence.quote: comprising all 21 Wolf-Rayets within the field of view, plus eight cool and 21 OB super-/hypergiants.

claims.hypothesis: Mass-loss rates increase through post-MS evolution
claims.experiment: Derive 3 mm free-free mass-loss rates for WR, OB, LBV stars
claims.result: WRs log Mdot -4.1 to -4.8; B super/hypergiants -5.1 to -5.8
claims.finding: Significant increase from OB supergiant to WR

evidence.loc: 8.1 Post-MS mass-loss rates and stellar evolution

claims.hypothesis: Hot stars' extended 3 mm emission is not the stellar wind
claims.experiment: Compare Gaussian sizes with analytic mm-photosphere radii

evidence.quote: As a consequence we may reject the hypothesis that we are resolving the stellar wind in any of these sources.

claims.hypothesis: Binarity does not make WRs systematically brighter, but Wd1-9 is extreme
claims.experiment: Compare binary and single WR mass-loss rates
claims.finding: Wd1-9 mass-loss comparable to most extreme WRs

evidence.quote: In general we find no evidence that massive binaries are systematically brighter than single stars due to an additional contribution from the wind-collision zone.

why_this_method.value: Free-free mm emission arises at large radii where terminal velocity reached, so less dependent on velocity law

evidence.quote: the emission due to electron-ion interactions in their ionised winds arises at large radii, where the terminal velocity will have been reached.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Binary or LBV ejection mechanisms and resolved WCRs rejected as explanation for extended hot-star emission

evidence.loc: 8.2 Resolved emission associated with the OB super/hyper-giant and WR cohorts
evidence.quote: it unlikely that we have resolved the (putative) WCRs of these objects.

limitations_admitted.value: Heterogeneous S/N precludes flux-limited survey; non-detections bias OB sample; mm flux of extended sources partly resolved out

evidence.quote: the heterogeneous S/N ratio across the field precludes consideration of our results as a flux-limited survey of OB stars within Wd1.
